associations.name: Caxcan
associations.associationType: Historical regional connection in specialist scholarship
associations.period: Early sixteenth century, including the period of Spanish arrival in 1531
associations.sourceTitle: Angélica María Medrano Enríquez — Prácticas funerarias en el territorio caxcán (Noroeste de México)
associations.sourceDate: Issue header July–December 2022; received January 15, 2024 and accepted March 15, 2024; publication-date discrepancy not resolved
associations.evidenceNote: The opening abstract explicitly places Caxcan communities in the south of present-day Zacatecas and the northwestern Los Altos area of Jalisco at Spanish arrival. This directly supports Mexico as a historical country-level index.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual PDF downloaded normally with valid TLS, HTTP 200; 27 pages available. Spanish and English introductory abstracts, printed pp.158–159 / PDF pp.1–2, inspected. No burial-site details, images or coordinates are used.
limits: Contemporary communities and recognition are not established by this historical abstract.
Only country-level navigation is proposed, not an exclusive territory.

associations.name: Cochimí
associations.associationType: Historical peninsula connection with identity-scope caveat
associations.period: Mission-era Baja California history, in a government record last modified 2019
associations.sourceTitle: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural — Cochimíes
associations.evidenceNote: The government cultural record explicitly associates Cochimí history with the Baja California peninsula and lists Baja California in its distribution field. This supports a broad Mexico route. The narrower implications of the identity label remain unresolved.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML geographic distribution and opening mission-history paragraphs, plus modification credit inspected (current extraction lines 264–287 and 308–311).
limits: The record juxtaposes historical Cochimí, Tipai identification at La Huerta and San Antonio Nécua, and descendants at Santa Gertrudis; these are not treated as automatically interchangeable.
No demographic count, extinction assertion, current leadership or language classification is adopted.
Country-level geography is supported; a more precise community/period account needs later review.

associations.name: Coree
associations.associationType: Historical community geography in a federal park account
associations.period: European-contact period and the early eighteenth century
associations.sourceTitle: National Park Service, Cape Lookout National Seashore — Native Americans of the South Outer Banks
associations.evidenceNote: The Coree discussion identifies Carteret and Craven counties in coastal North Carolina and explicitly locates Coree communities near Cape Lookout at European contact. This establishes a historical North Carolina connection.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML And Who Were the Coree? paragraphs, lines 24–29, inspected.
limits: The source explicitly acknowledges uncertainty about language and cultural classification.
Archaeological site attribution, disappearance assertions and equivalence with Tuscarora, Machapunga or Neusiok are not adopted.
No burial information or site coordinates are reproduced.

associations.name: Kitsai
associations.associationType: Specific Kichai-descendant community and shared-government connection
associations.period: Community historical account of the period from 1934 onward; present-page institutional location
associations.sourceTitle: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes — A New Beginning: 1934–Present
associations.evidenceNote: The Tribe identifies Kichai descendants among its constituent peoples and explicitly places its community and government center at Anadarko, Oklahoma. Lesser and Weltfish’s original naming footnote identifies Kitsai as their spelling of Kichai. Together these support an Oklahoma connection with the alias explained.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual tribal page lines 30–35 and 44–46 inspected. Supporting 1932 Smithsonian PDF title and printed p.1 / PDF p.5, especially naming footnote, read as text/OCR.
limits: Kitsai/Kichai and Wichita remain distinct historical people/language names within a shared government setting.
No language-loss statement is used to infer disappearance of descendants.
The historical account is not treated as an audit of current government rules.

supportingSources.title: Alexander Lesser and Gene Weltfish — Composition of the Caddoan Linguistic Stock
supportingSources.scope: Printed p.1 / PDF p.5 naming footnote only, plus title-page identification; no full-work or contemporary-language review claimed.

associations.name: Kwakwaka'wakw
associations.sourceTitle: U’mista Cultural Society — location and mandate
associations.evidenceNote: The Society explicitly states that it is located in Alert Bay, British Columbia, and that its mandate concerns the cultural heritage of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw. This is a direct British Columbia institutional connection.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual homepage introductory sentence, line 10, plus About Us mandate and society paragraphs, lines 9–17, inspected. The explicit facility location, not incorporation under provincial law alone, supplies the geographic tie.
limits: This collective name encompasses distinct communities and nations. The Society is not presented as one government for them all.
No ceremonial narratives, regalia images, sales listings or permissions to reuse cultural material are adopted.

supportingSources.title: U’mista Cultural Centre — About Us
supportingSources.scope: Mandate and Society paragraphs only; no exhibitions or origin narratives reviewed.

associations.name: Massachusett
associations.associationType: Historical homeland described by a continuing community
associations.period: Before and during early European colonial arrival
associations.sourceTitle: Massachusett Tribe at Ponkapoag — The History of the Neponset Band of the Indigenous Massachusett Tribe
associations.evidenceNote: The community’s history explicitly places Indigenous Massachusett villages in what is now the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, describing a coastal and inland range using Salem, Plymouth and Worcester. This directly supports a Massachusetts historical connection.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual opening geographic and community paragraphs, HTML lines 55–57, inspected.
limits: The Neponset/Ponkapoag community account is attributed to its publisher, not treated as the only Massachusett perspective.
No state/federal recognition determination, epidemic percentage or exact historical boundary is adopted.

associations.name: Métis
associations.associationType: Specific Métis government and community connection
associations.sourceTitle: Métis Nation–Saskatchewan — About the Métis Nation
associations.sourceDate: Undated live page; old governance URL redirects to this institutional page
associations.evidenceNote: Métis Nation–Saskatchewan explicitly identifies itself as a government representing Métis citizens in Saskatchewan. The same page describes the Métis as a distinct Indigenous people. This supports a specific Saskatchewan route without making this government equivalent to all Métis communities.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML body lines 9–17 and institutional address context, lines 23–26, inspected. Original metisnationsk.com/governance/ redirected to mns.ca.
limits: The institution’s membership definition and wider homeland account are not applied as universal eligibility rules.
Métis identity is not used as a generic synonym for any person with mixed ancestry.
No exclusive territorial boundary or claim to represent all Métis political perspectives is made.

associations.name: Mobile
associations.associationType: Historical people and village geography in specialist scholarship
associations.period: Mobile Bay communities around French settlement in 1702
associations.sourceTitle: John J. Gurner — French in Alabama: 1699–1763 (Encyclopedia of Alabama)
associations.evidenceNote: The account identifies Mobile among Indigenous peoples of the Mobile Bay area in 1702 and separately describes the French settlement near a Mobilian village. This supplies an Alabama historical connection through explicit people/village evidence, rather than through the later city name alone.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual geography/context and settlement paragraphs, HTML lines 70–88, plus named Mobile people passage at line 95 and author/date credit at 151–161 inspected.
limits: Mobile people, the colonial town and the modern city are distinct referents.
This does not establish present government continuity, a census or equivalence with all speakers of Mobilian trade language.

The discovered 2018 Voss article associates Acalan (Mactun) with southern Campeche in indexed text, but direct HTML and PDF web reads timed out. It is retained as a lead rather than a confirmed association.
unresolved.namingCaution: Keep the exact canonical access point Mactun. Indexed UNAM p.181 interprets amactún / mactún uinicob as historical self-designations of Acalán Chontal Maya. This is not evidence for inventing a separate present-day nation. Homonymous modern place names or weather stations do not prove identity.
